ei.title: Chapter 1-04 2번: The Evolutionary Impact of Cooking Food
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: Cooked food does many familiar things. It makes our food safer, creates delicious tastes, and reduces the risk of going bad. Heating can allow us to open, cut, or mash tough foods. But none of these advantages is as important as a little-appreciated aspect: cooking increases the amount of energy our bodies obtain from our food. The extra energy gave the first cooks biological advantages. They survived and reproduced better than before. Their genes spread. Their bodies responded by biologically adapting to cooked food, shaped by natural selection to take maximum advantage of the new diet. There were changes in anatomy, physiology, ecology, life history, psychology, and society. Fossil evidence indicates that this dependence arose not just some tens of thousands of years ago, but right back at the beginning of our time on Earth, at the start of human evolution. We should indeed pin our humanity on cooks.

Their bodies responded by biologically adapting to cooked food, shaped by natural selection to take maximum advantage of the new diet. There were changes in anatomy, physiology, ecology, life history, psychology, and society. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 요리는 상하는 위험을 줄이고(reduces), 우리 몸이 에너지를 얻고(obtain), 최초의 요리사에게 생물학적 이점(advantages)을 주었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① reduces — obtain — advantages — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② increases — obtain — advantages (A 반대: 줄이다→늘리다)
❌ ③ reduces — release — advantages (B 반대: 얻다→방출하다)
❌ ④ reduces — obtain — drawbacks (C 반대: 이점→단점)

det.korean: 그들은 생존했고(survived), 조리된 음식에 적응하며(adapting), 최대한의(maximum) 이점을 취했다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② survived — resisting — maximum (B 반대: 적응하다→저항하다)
❌ ③ survived — adapting — minimum (C 반대: 최대→최소)

② tough — 질긴, 원문 일치
③ abandon — 원문은 obtain(얻다) ←정답

② spread — 퍼지다, 원문 일치
③ responded — 반응하다, 원문 일치

questions.passage: Cooked food does many familiar things. It makes our food safer, creates delicious tastes, and reduces the risk of going bad. Heating can allow us to open, cut, or mash tough foods. But none of these advantages is as important as a little-appreciated aspect: cooking increases the amount of energy our bodies obtain from our food. The extra energy gave the first cooks biological advantages. They survived and reproduced better than before. Their genes spread. Their bodies responded by biologically adapting to cooked food, shaped by natural selection to take maximum advantage of the new diet.
